title: Bellman equations as linear algebra
brief: Turn a policy into a Markov chain, solve for its values exactly, derive action values, and compute the discounted state-visitation distribution.
hints: np.einsum('sa,sat->st', pi, mdp.P) averages the transition rows over the policy's actions. The expected reward is (pi * mdp.R).sum(axis=1).
Zero the terminal rows with a mask: live = ~mdp.terminal, then P_pi * live[:, None] and r_pi * live.
Solve, don't invert: np.linalg.solve(np.eye(S) - mdp.gamma * P_pi, r_pi).
mdp.P @ v has shape (S, A): entry [s, a] is the expected next-state value. Add mdp.R and scale by gamma for Q.
The visitation distribution is a row vector on the left, so solve the transposed system: np.linalg.solve((I - gamma P_pi).T, mu0).
